# AuthenticationServices

**Symbols:** 28.6% of Apple's iOS API (417 of 1460, exact) · **Rows:** 13: 9 ✅ 4 ❌ · **iOS:** 12.0+

**Area:** [Identity & security](../COVERAGE.md#security) · **Apple:** [AuthenticationServices](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/authenticationservices) · **Issues:** [`area:security`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Asecurity)

## How isim implements it

- **Adapted:**
  - Sign in with Apple uses a local account and an unsigned JWT;
  - `ASWebAuthenticationSession` runs on isim's WKWebView;
  - passkeys are CryptoKit P-256 keys in the device data;
  - app extensions (credential providers, SSO, account modification) run in the process of the app that asks, as
    isim's share and keyboard extensions do; on iOS each runs in its own process.

|---|---|---|---|
| Sign in with Apple (`ASAuthorizationAppleIDProvider`, `ASAuthorizationController`, `ASAuthorizationAppleIDButton`, `SignInWithAppleButton`) | ✅ | ≤17 | **local simulation, no Apple servers**: iOS-style sheet (Apple ID / Apple Account wording by `ISIM_OS_VERSION`, name, Share/Hide My Email, Continue/close) for a fake account in the device data; returning users get the short sheet without name/email. `identityToken` is an **unsigned JWT (`alg: none`, issuer `isim-local-simulation`)** and `authorizationCode` a random local string — servers that verify Apple signatures reject them. `getCredentialState` authorized/revoked/notFound per app; `isim appleid <app> revoke` posts `credentialRevokedNotification` to the running app. Buttons: black/white/whiteOutline, sign in/continue/sign up, isim-drawn logo. Tested: HelloSignIn |
| `ASWebAuthenticationSession` (OAuth) | ✅ | ≤17 | iOS's “Wants to Use … to Sign In” alert (skipped when ephemeral), the page in a browser sheet on isim's WKWebView (real WebKit), callback by custom scheme or (iOS 17.4) https host+path — links, forms and server redirects; Cancel → `canceledLogin`; `presentationContextProvider` errors; SwiftUI `webAuthenticationSession` environment action. Tested against a local OAuth page (HelloSafari). Non-ephemeral sessions share SFSafariViewController's in-memory data, not Safari's |
| Passkeys (`ASAuthorizationPlatformPublicKeyCredentialProvider` registration + assertion) | ✅ | ≤17 | real WebAuthn data: P-256 key (CryptoKit), CBOR attestation object with format `none` (AAGUID zero, COSE key), clientDataJSON with origin `https://<rp>`, assertion signature over authData ‖ SHA-256(clientDataJSON) that verifies. Keys kept unencrypted in the device data (not synced). iOS-style save/sign-in sheets; no passkey → canceled (no nearby-device QR); `preferImmediatelyAvailableCredentials` → `notInteractive`. Security keys (`ASAuthorizationSecurityKey…`), PRF/large blob missing. Tested: HelloSignIn |
| Password sign-in (`ASAuthorizationPasswordProvider`, `ASPasswordCredential`), AutoFill-assisted requests | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: the chooser sheet offers the app's internet passwords from isim's keychain and the device's Passwords store (filled by UIKit's QuickType AutoFill bar and "Save Password?", for the app's `webcredentials:` domains); `performAutoFillAssistedRequests` shows no sheet and offers the relying party's passkeys in the QuickType bar of `.username` fields, picking one completes the request (passkey assertion requests only, like iOS). No iCloud Keychain sync. Tested: HelloSignIn, test_text_services |
| Passkey extensions: PRF (`ASAuthorizationPublicKeyCredentialPRFRegistrationInput` / `…PRFAssertionInput` with `InputValues`, `…PRFRegistrationOutput` / `…PRFAssertionOutput`) and largeBlob (`ASAuthorizationPublicKeyCredentialLargeBlobRegistrationInput` / `…AssertionInput`, their outputs), the `prf` / `largeBlob` properties of the platform requests and credentials | ✅ | 17.0 | adapted (largeBlob iOS 17, PRF iOS 18): each passkey gets a random 32-byte PRF secret when it is created, and an evaluation is HMAC-SHA-256(secret, SHA-256("WebAuthn PRF" ‖ 0x00 ‖ salt)), as WebAuthn defines it, so a credential and salt always give the same key (per-credential salts win over the default ones). The large blob (up to 2 KiB) is kept with the passkey in the device data. The Objective-C classes are Apple's (`__ASAuthorization…` in Swift). Tested: HelloSignIn (tests/ui/test_signin.py: the same PRF key at registration and sign-in, a blob written then read back from the QuickType bar), HelloAuthObjC |
| Security keys (`ASAuthorizationSecurityKeyPublicKeyCredentialProvider`, its registration and assertion requests and credentials, `ASAuthorizationSecurityKeyPublicKeyCredentialDescriptor` with `Transport`, `ASAuthorizationPublicKeyCredentialParameters`, `ASCOSEAlgorithmIdentifier`, `ASAuthorizationPublicKeyCredentialResidentKeyPreference`, the `appID` extension, PRF) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: a virtual USB security key whose credentials (P-256, attestation "none", PRF secret) are kept in the device data (`Library/isim/SecurityKey/<relying party>.json`). Registration shows a "Set Up a Security Key" sheet where iOS asks to insert a key; sign-ins list the key's credentials in the chooser ("Security key · <site>"): the allowed ones (also those registered under the request's `appID`, which sets `appID` on the assertion), else the discoverable ones (`residentKeyPreference` other than `.discouraged`). ES256 only; `excludedCredentials` matches fail with `matchedExcludedCredential`. No real security keys (USB, NFC, Bluetooth). Tested: HelloSignIn, HelloAuthObjC |
| Conditional passkey registration (`ASAuthorizationPlatformPublicKeyCredentialRegistrationRequest.RequestStyle`, `requestStyle`, `createCredentialRegistrationRequest(challenge:name:userID:requestStyle:)`) | ✅ | 18.0 | adapted: a `.conditional` request shows no sheet. It creates the passkey when the app's saved passwords (keychain internet passwords, the device's Passwords store) have one for the account `name`; iOS also requires that password to have been used just before, which isim doesn't track. Otherwise it fails with `ASAuthorizationError.failed` (proposed: Apple doesn't document the code). After it, a "Passkey Saved" notification banner appears at the top of the screen (accessibility identifier `as-banner`). `excludedCredentials` are honoured for every passkey registration. Tested: HelloSignIn (refused without a saved password, then created with the banner; iOS 17: unavailable), HelloAuthObjC |
| SwiftUI `AuthorizationController` (`EnvironmentValues.authorizationController`: `performRequest(s)`, with `options:`, `customMethods:`, `performAutoFillAssistedRequest(s)`), `ASAuthorizationResult`, `ASAuthorizationCustomMethod` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: an `ASAuthorizationController` run from the key window, its result as an `ASAuthorizationResult` (or the error thrown). Custom methods are tvOS-only, so none are offered, as on iOS. `ASAuthorizationController.customAuthorizationMethods` is now `[ASAuthorizationCustomMethod]`; apps built before still reach the old `[Any]` property. Missing: `ASAuthorizationResult.passkeyAccountCreation` (iOS 26: its credential type is not in isim). Tested: HelloSignIn (a security key through `authorizationController`) |

The extension (`com.apple.AppSSO.idp-extension`) runs in the app; the identity provider URL gets the request's scope, state, nonce and options as query items. `complete(httpAuthorizationHeaders:)` gives an `authenticatedResponse` with those headers; `complete(httpResponse:httpBody:)` gives the response, with `access_token` / `id_token` from a JSON body. `doNotHandle()` fails with `.notHandled`, as does a URL no profile covers. Not intercepted: Safari, WebKit and URLSession requests to the identity provider. Platform SSO (`ASAuthorizationProviderExtensionLoginManager`) is macOS-only.
